correctness.rationale: Geometric fixed points correspond to barycentric orbit subsets, where complement of chosen orbits must contain d vertices in at least one part. This is a disjunction of orbit-weight budget inequalities <=a_i−d, equivalent by Alexander duality to E=(E1*...*Ek)^vee where E_i is weight<=d−1. The Alexander dual of a join is union of two cones with intersection the join of individual duals, giving Σ^{k−1}(Q1*...*Qk) in augmented interpretation. In each Q_i the least-weight vertex closed star is contractible; every face outside it with T−u_min<weight(B)<=T is maximal and attaches by its whole boundary, yielding wedge S^{|B|−1}. Join and suspension dimensions give β_j=[z^{j−k+2}]∏ P_i(z), integral free homology and complete wedge type. Boundary when a part<d is contractible or empty as claimed. For K_{9,4}, d=4, weights (1,1,2,2,3) and (4), P1=2z²+z³ and P2=1, giving 2S² ∨ S³. Independent direct orbit-face GF2 boundary calculations for small profiles and claimed example matched; infinite homotopy proof is structural.
